name: Mambae
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 further work by the same author (or citing it for stress) agrees.

new_statements.quote: O acento lexical em Mambae ocorre sempre na sílaba à esquerda do pé métrico. Isso significa que o penúltimo segmento vocálico é acentudado. Portanto, não distingue palavras. Uma vogal acentuada é comumente realizada com intensidade aumentada e de duração um pouco maior se comparada com vogais não acentuadas. A sílaba acentuada é identificada por *ơ. [p. 118–119] … O modelo para a palavra prosódica mínima é formada de um um pé binário, de cabeça esquerda (133), onde P representa o pé métrico, A representa a sílaba acentuada e Na a sílaba não acentuada. [p. 114]
new_statements.translation: Lexical stress in Mambae always falls on the left-hand syllable of the metrical foot. This means that the penultimate vowel segment is stressed. Therefore it does not distinguish words. A stressed vowel is commonly realized with increased intensity and slightly greater duration compared with unstressed vowels. The stressed syllable is marked *ơ. [pp. 118–119] … The template for the minimal prosodic word is formed of a binary, left-headed foot (133), where P is the metrical foot, A the stressed syllable and Na the unstressed syllable. [p. 114]
new_statements.citation: Fogaça, Helem Andressa de Oliveira. 2017. O ecossistema fundamental da língua Mambae. PhD thesis, Universidade de Brasília, 297 pp.
new_statements.locator: §4.5 'Acento Lexical', pp. 118–119 (PDF pages 118–119, printed page numbers match); foot template §4.4.5, p. 114; trisyllable table 4.12, p. 116; syncope §4.6.1.1, p. 120
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (297 pp., text present; extracted text pages 114-121). §4.5 'Acento Lexical' begins at the foot of p. 118 and continues on p. 119: 'O acento lexical em Mambae ocorre sempre na sílaba à esquerda do pé métrico. Isso significa que o penúltimo segmento vocálico é acentudado. Portanto, não distingue palavras. Uma vogal acentuada é comumente realizada com intensidade aumentada e de duração um pouco maior se comparada com vogais não acentuadas. A sílaba acentuada é identificada por *ơ.' — verbatim, typos included; examples (141)-(144) ˈli.im 'cinco', ˈhu.a 'coração', ˈbru.is 'quente', anˈka.te 'criança' as reported. The p. 114 sentence 'O modelo para a palavra prosódica mínima é formada de…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog penultimate stress = stress on the penult at every length; Fogaça 2017 says the same (penultimate vowel, left-headed binary foot) and adds: stress is non-contrastive, its phonetic cues (intensity, slight length), the foot/word template (one foot plus at most one unfooted initial syllable), unstressed monosyllabic function words, stress stability under syncope, and that words longer than three syllables are only compounds/loans.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is on the penultimate syllable (the penultimate vowel: every vowel, including each half of a VV sequence, is a syllable nucleus, so li.im 'five', hu.a 'heart', bru.is 'hot' stress the first vowel). Words are one left-headed (trochaic) binary foot, optionally preceded by one unfooted syllable, so disyllables stress the first syllable and trisyllables the second (basˈkari 'scatter', faˈnao 'steal', naˈbilan 'shine', anˈkate 'child'); stress is non-contrastive. Cues: greater intensity and slightly longer duration.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed. Four-syllable words occur only as compounds or loans (p. 118); the compound examples on p. 120 show each root keeping its own stress (/ˈana ˈmaɛn/ → [anˈmaɛn] 'boy', /ˈɛra ˈtiris/ → [ɛɾˈtiɾis] 'waterfall'), i.e. surface stress lands on the penult of the compound after apocope.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for native words. Monosyllabic function words (ba negator, prepositions ma, la, relativizer ke) are smaller than a foot and unstressed (p. 118). Syncope of the first-syllable vowel in trisyllables (faˈnao > fˈnao) does not move the stress (p. 120). Loans from Portuguese/Indonesian may have a coda in the penult (p. 114) but no stress deviation is stated for them.
new_statements.identity_note: Fogaça 2017 describes 'Mambae Sul' (South Mambae) as spoken in the administrative post of Same, Manufahi (p. 24: 'uma descrição endoecológia específica do Mambae Sul, falado no posto administrativo de Same'), with cross-reference to other Mambae varieties (Ainaro, Aileu, Ermera) surveyed lexically in ch. 3.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the cited 2013 MA dissertation at the cited places (sec. 4.3 pp. 61-62 and Conclusion p. 77), now downloaded and held by the project (previously no copy. 'grade' field is blank). The source is a first-hand phonological study, and the same author's 2017 PhD thesis (297 pp, the best available description per Glottolog, also downloaded) independently restates the rule: stress 'sempre na penúltima sílaba', non-contrastive, realised by intensity and duration. Coding 'penult, fixed-dominant (non-strict)' with penultimate stress is correct: penult is the regular locus; exceptions are Portuguese oxytone loans (2013 p. 65; 2017 ex. 166) and, for the Ainaro dialect, Hull's acute-marked irregular words (medéd, batár, reported via Fogaça 2013 p. 23). sources.quote: O padrão predominante no Mambae é o que Hayes (COLLISCHONN, 1999, pg 130) denomina como troqueu silábico ... um pé dissilábico com proeminência inicial, que conta as sílabas, mas ignora sua estrutura interna. ... O acento primário das palavras geralmente recai sobre a penúltima sílaba.
